newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban order Iranian embassy in Kabul to close.
newsitem.headline: Taleban order Iranian embassy in Kabul to close.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban militia on Monday ordered the Iranian embassy in Kabul to close for alleged involvement in espionage, a Taleban spokesman said.

Wakil Ahmad, a senior Taleban official in the southern city of Kandahar, told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) that the embassy had been "gathering wrong information" about Afghanistan and was not neutral in the Afghan conflict.
Ahmad said the Iranian press had been giving "wrong information" about Afghanistan and Tehran was not in favour of reconciliation with the Taleban government in Kabul.
"Therefore, the government has ordered the embassy closed until the situation becomes normal in the country and until further notice," AIP quoted Ahmad as saying.
It was not immediately clear whether Iranian diplomats stationed in Kabul had already left the capital.

The Iranian embassy has been among the very few diplomatic missions to remain open in Kabul throughout the factional fighting that has plagued the city since Islamic guerrilla forces ousted the former communist government in 1992.
